notes: porter declared unbuildable after 1 attempt(s): The `recursion` program's provable body IS the Jolt verifier running inside the guest: it deserializes a `JoltVerifierPreprocessing<F, Curve, PCS>`, then N `RV64IMACProof`/`JoltDevice` pairs, and calls `RV64IMACVerifier::verify()`. Lifting that body requires `jolt-sdk` with the `guest-verifier` feature, which is *defined* as `guest-verifier = ["guest-std", "dep:common", "jolt-core/minimal"]`, and `guest-std = ["postcard/use-std", "jolt-platform/std", "jolt-sdk-macros/guest-std", "serde/std", "zeroos-std"]` where `zeroos-std = ["dep:zeroos", "zeroos-runtime-musl"]`. i.e. the in-guest verifier has NO no_std path by construction — it is only buildable in ZeroOS musl/std mode. Confirmed at the crate level: `jolt-core/src/lib.rs` carries no `#![no_std]` attribute under any feature, so `jolt-core/minimal` is an unconditional std crate; there is no `core`/`alloc` equivalent to substitute and no feature-flag repoint that keeps the dependency graph no_std. The corpus guest also enables `jolt_sdk` features `thread` (zeroos cooperative scheduler) and `random` (zeroos RNG) — both OS-capability/entropy features forbidden in a deterministic no_std guest. Forcing this to build would require switching the frozen template to std/musl mode, which is explicitly prohibited (it changes the study target). Secondary, independently fatal blockers: (a) the provable body is wrapped in `provable_with_config!` from `src/provable_macro.rs` and reads `embedded_bytes::EMBEDDED_BYTES` from `src/embedded_bytes.rs` — NEITHER file exists in the read-only corpus tree; both are generated at runtime by the benchmark's own host (`cargo run -- verify --example <x> --embed`), which first runs a full prove pipeline. Without them the lifted code has no input data at all, and the fallback `build.rs` emits an EMPTY `EMBEDDED_BYTES`, which makes the body fall through to `bytes` and immediately `unwrap()`-panic on deserializing preprocessing from a short slice. (b) Memory config is irreconcilable with the frozen harness attribute: the benchmark requires `heap_size` 33,554,432–134,217,728, `stack_size` 4,194,304–33,554,432, `max_input_size` up to 2,000,000, and `max_trace_length` up to 67,108,864; the template's frozen line is `#[jolt::provable(heap_size = 32768, max_trace_length = 65536)]` (default 4096-byte input), ~4000x too small in heap and ~1000x too short in trace, and I must not edit it. (c) The body uses `std::io::Cursor` as the ark-serialize reader, which is a repoint-able detail only if (a)–(b) and the jolt-core std dependency were solvable — they are not. No algorithm-preserving port exists; no files were modified.
